Good catch — that's the right instinct to have. Here's where that leaves it:

**Corroboration: not real, despite the appearance of three sources.** All three posts tracing back to the same GitHub issue (#4521) means you have one source wearing three hats, not three independent confirmations. Three people writing about the same root report doesn't add evidence weight beyond what that root report itself carries — it just adds visibility.

**The underlying claim itself: unverified.** I haven't seen issue #4521 — don't know who filed it, whether it's from a maintainer with a repro case, a single user's anecdote, whether it's been triaged/labeled, or whether anyone's confirmed it against our specific version and config. That's the actual thing that matters here, and none of the three blog posts give you independent evidence on it — they're just relaying the same claim.

So: "seems pretty solid" doesn't hold up as stated. What would actually move this from unverified to something real is looking at the issue itself — who raised it, what evidence/repro is attached, whether it's been reproduced by someone else independently (not just linked by someone else). If you can get me the issue content or a link, I can actually assess it instead of just flagging that the three-source appearance is hollow.
